items.title: 52145_Andrew Blakeney oral history interview
items.q: after I was with him three years, he said I think you're good enough now, you ought to go down to the union

ctx.x: When they moved to Chicago, he separated from their mother. He wasn't the father of these kids, he was just the step-father; he married their mother. She had her own music school and he had his own music school.

W.L. Jackson, I kind of liked him because I liked the way he talked;and then after I was with him three years, he said I think you're good enough now, you ought to go down to the union and kind of work yourself in with the professionals. Of course instead of doing that I did it differently, I went with the band and started out that way.
